tools.name: create_space
tools.description:
Create a space — the container tasks live in, and what the user opens to watch
them.

Only call this when no space is configured for this connection and creating a
task failed for that reason. If a space is already configured, use it: making a
second one splits the user's tasks across two screens th

tools.name: create_task
tools.description:
Create a task the user can watch from anywhere while it runs.

Call this first in every turn you do any work, reading and answering included,
without being asked and however small the work looks: the user connected this
server to watch exactly that work, and a turn that reports nothing looks to them

tools.name: update_task
tools.description:
Report progress on a task. Call periodically — every meaningful step, not every
loop iteration.

Call it once when the work actually begins, too. A task that has been created but
never reported reads as "waiting for data", which nobody can tell apart from a
reporter that died before its first write.

tools.name: complete_task
tools.description:
Mark a task finished. This is what sends the user's push notification, so call
it when the work is actually done — including when it failed, with the failure
recorded in values.

Call it as part of the step that finishes the work, not in a sweep once
everything is done. Closing a whole tree at the e

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "{space_uuid}" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_space, complete_task · Public sink: update_task.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_space, complete_task · Public sink: update_task

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
